rules.title: FEHA source-of-income and government-subsidy screening limits
rules.requirement: Where there is a government rent subsidy, a housing provider may not use a financial or income standard that is not based on the portion of the rent the tenant pays. If a provider uses credit history, it must let the applicant offer lawful, verifiable alternative evidence of ability to pay the tenant's portion (benefit payments, pay records, bank statements). It must give reasonable time to respond and reasonably consider that evidence in place of credit history. Income standards must also count the aggregate income of persons residing together on the same basis as married persons. 'Source of income' includes public assistance and housing subsidies such as Section 8 and HUD-VASH vouchers. Owners may still verify employment, request landlord references and verify identity.

coverage.summary: Applies to the rental of housing generally; the passages state no unit-count or building-age limits.
coverage.other_conditions: Subsidy-specific income and credit rules apply where there is a government rent subsidy.

rules.effective_date_note: The passages give no effective date.
rules.quoted_span: (A) Use a financial or income standard in assessing eligibility for the rental of housing that is not based on the portion of the rent to be paid by the tenant.
rules.review_note: The passages show only subdivisions (n)-(p) of an unnamed 'section'. The Gov. Code § 12955 citation is inferred, not stated in the text. The CRD FAQ (D016) says refusing to rent based on source of income is prohibited.

rules.title: Criminal history screening limits (Civil Rights Council fair housing regulations)
rules.requirement: Housing providers may not consider arrests that did not lead to a conviction, sealed or expunged records, or juvenile justice records. Blanket bans on applicants with a criminal history are prohibited. A denial based on a conviction must be directly related to being a good tenant and not a threat to others' health, safety or property. The provider should weigh the nature and severity of the crime and the time elapsed.

coverage.summary: Applies to housing providers generally; the passages state no size or age limits.

rules.effective_date_note: A secondary source (CAA) says the Civil Rights Council regulations took effect Jan. 1, 2020.
citation_aliases: Civil Rights Council criminal history regulations
rules.quoted_span: Housing providers cannot consider some types of criminal history including arrests that did not lead to a conviction, records that are sealed or expunged, or records or matters processed in the juvenile justice system.
rules.review_note: The passages do not name the regulation sections. The citation is inferred and should be verified. The description comes from a CRD FAQ and a CAA article, not the regulation text.
rules.source_notes: Corroborated by a CAA article (DX07) describing the regulations: blanket bans prohibited, arrests without convictions not considered.
